column2: Enjoy it
You get free coffee for a week. The crew calls you 'Hollywood'.
Cold Water Training
Mandatory cold water training in Alaska. The water is 38 degrees. The instructor says to swim 200 meters. What do you do?
Go hard and fast
You finish before your hands stop working.
Your muscles seize at 150 meters.
Pace yourself
Steady and smart. You finish.
Too slow. Your body gives out.
Drug Run Witness
On a patrol flight, you spot a go-fast boat dumping bales overboard. The crew asks you to keep eyes on it. What do you do?
Track the bales
A cutter recovers 2,000 pounds of cocaine. Your sharp eyes get credit.
Track the boat
The cutter stops the boat. Arrests made.
It outruns everyone.
You pull your back deadlifting. If you report it, you're off the duty schedule. The station is short-handed. What do you do?
Two weeks of rehab. You come back stronger.
It goes out during a hoist. Now it's serious.
Bad Weather Joke
On a stormy night, the senior swimmer says the coffee is so bad it's a hazmat case. Everyone laughs. He asks you to make better coffee. What do you do?
Make great coffee
Your coffee becomes station legend.
Somehow, it's worse.
Order energy drinks
Everyone is jittery. Mission accomplished.
A man in the water slipped from your grip just as the hoist lifted. Another crew found him an hour later, deceased. What do you do?
Talk to the senior swimmer
He tells you about his worst day. You feel less alone.
Blame yourself
You replay it every night.
Request a debrief
The debrief finds a technique fix. It helps.
A Category 4 hurricane is coming. Your station is evacuating aircraft, but swimmers will stay and fly after landfall. Your family wants you home. What do you do?
Stay with the crew
You get your family to a shelter, then report.
Help family evacuate first
You make it back just in time.
You're late. The chief is furious.
Survival Suit Fail
Your dry suit has a leak and you're slowly filling with freezing water. You're mid-rescue. What do you do?
Finish the rescue
You get the survivor up, then shiver for an hour.
Hypothermia sets in. You both need to be hoisted together.
Call for re-hoist
A second swimmer takes over. Everyone lives.
Liberty in Kodiak
Liberty in Kodiak. There are exactly two bars. {buddy} wants to go to the one where the fishermen fight. What do you do?
The calm bar
Quiet night. You hear about the fight the next morning.
The fight bar
The fishermen buy you drinks after hearing you're a swimmer.
You get dragged into a brawl. NJP.
In the dunker training, the helicopter mock-up flips and fills with water. Your seat belt is stuck. What do you do?
Stay calm and feel it
You find the buckle and get out.
Safety divers pull you out.
Somehow, you get free.
Safety divers have to rescue the rescuer.
Night Vision Training
Your first night hoist using NVGs. Depth perception is terrible and the water looks like black glass. What do you do?
Trust the mech
He talks you down perfectly.
You hit the water harder than expected.
Go by feel
It works.
You misjudge the distance.
Your partner wants to get married before your next PCS move to Alaska. You've dated eight months. What do you do?
Married. Alaska is less lonely now.
The marriage struggles in the dark Alaska winters.
Long distance is hard.
Crab Boat Sinking
A crab boat is sinking in the Bering Sea at night. 30-foot seas, 20 degrees out. Six crew in survival suits are scattered in the water. What do you do?
Get them in pairs
Exhausting, but all six come home.
A wave throws you into the hull. You still get four.
Prioritize the closest
You get five. A cutter finds the last one alive.
You get five. The sixth is lost.
Use the basket alone
Efficient. All six out.
The basket swings and hits a survivor.
A hiker fell onto a ledge on a sea cliff. Waves are pounding the base. The helo can't get close because of the cliff. What do you do?
The pilot holds a perfect hover. Hiker out.
The rotor wash knocks rocks loose. You're hit.
Climb from the water
Incredible climb. Hiker out.
A wave slams you into the cliff.
Wait for a cliff team
Local climbers reach him in two hours. He's fine.
An overloaded migrant boat capsizes in the Florida Straits. 25 people in the water, many can't swim. You're the only swimmer. What do you do?
Throw flotation, triage
Rafts deployed. A cutter arrives. Most survive.
Some slip away before help arrives.
Grab the children first
You get every child. The cutter saves the adults.
You save the kids. Some adults are lost.
Floodwaters are at the roofline. A family of five is on a roof. Grandma is in a wheelchair and refuses to leave without her dog. What do you do?
Take the dog too
Grandma and the dog are hoisted in the basket together.
Insist on no dog
She comes, crying. A boat team rescues the dog later.
Cut through the roof
You chop into the attic to reach a trapped child too.
The roof is unstable. You slip.
You're now the senior swimmer at your station. A junior swimmer is good but cocky. He's making risky choices. What do you do?
He listens. He becomes a great swimmer.
He laughs it off.
Pull him off the schedule
He sulks. Then he listens.
A sailor on a cutter has a severe head injury. The ship is rolling heavily. You must lower to the deck in the dark. What do you do?
Time the rolls
Perfect timing. Patient out.
The deck comes up fast and slams you.
Use a trail line
The deck crew guides you in.
The line tangles.
You reach a fisherman who's been in the water three hours. He's barely conscious. If you lift him vertically, his heart may stop. What do you do?
Horizontal basket lift
Gentle lift. He survives.
His heart stops anyway. You do CPR all the way in.
Quick strop lift
He survives.
Rescue collapse. He dies in the cabin.
A sailboat in a storm 200 miles out lost its mast. The couple aboard are elderly and terrified. What do you do?
Get them in the water
You tow them from the boat one at a time. Safe.
The wife panics in the water and pulls you under.
Deck hoist
Quick lift from the deck.
The rigging tangles your cable.
Strobe in the Dark
A shrimp boat sank at night. Searchlights show nothing but whitecaps. The crew may only have a weak strobe. How do you search?
Lights off, NVGs on
Under goggles, a tiny strobe blazes like a star. Three men saved.
Fog swallows everything. A cutter finds them at dawn.
Drop flares and orbit
A man waves an arm in the flare light. Found.
The flares drift. Nothing.
Cruise Ship Overboard
A cruise passenger went overboard at night. The ship took an hour to turn around. The ocean is huge. How do you plan the search?
Trust the drift model
Right where the computer said. He's clinging to a deck chair, alive.
The current shifted. He's never found.
Search the ship's track
You spot him in the wake line. Unbelievable.
Hours of empty water.
Surfer on the Rocks
A surfer with a broken leg is pinned in rocks at the base of a point break. Twelve-foot sets keep burying him. What do you do?
Swim in between sets
You time the lull perfectly and drag him out to the hoist.
A rogue set catches you both. You get him out, bruised and bleeding.
Direct hoist from above
Fast extraction. The pilot holds steady as a rock.
The cable swings you into the rocks.
A smuggler's go-fast boat flipped during a chase. You're pulling him out, but he keeps trying to swim away from you. What do you do?
He realizes you're the only thing keeping him alive. He calms.
He elbows you in the face. You get him anyway.
Control hold and strop
You get behind him and lock him in. Up he goes.
He drags you under twice before you secure him.
Twenty ice fishermen are stranded on a floe that broke off on Lake Erie. It's cracking. The ice is too thin to land on. What do you do?
Hoist from a hover
Two helos and an airboat get everyone off before dark.
A slab tips you into the water. You climb out frozen.
Walk out with an ice sled
Faster. Everyone's off.
You punch through the ice up to your chest.
Faces at Night
You can't stop seeing the faces of people you couldn't reach. You're drinking more and snapping at your kids. What do you do?
It's hard to talk about. It helps more than you expected.
Keep it in
It gets worse. Your spouse notices before you do.
He's carrying the same weight. You lift it together.
You're offered an instructor billet at A-School in Elizabeth City. It's prestigious, but you'd stop flying cases for three years. What do you do?
You get to break, then build, the next generation of swimmers.
Keep flying
You stay operational. Your station is glad.
Captain Won't Leave
A fishing boat captain refuses to abandon his sinking boat. 'It's my whole life,' he yells. His crew is already in the water. What do you do?
Crew first, then him
Crew saved. He finally jumps as the stern goes under. You get him.
Board and drag him off
You physically haul him into the water. He thanks you later.
The boat rolls with you on it. You barely get clear.
Talk him off by radio
His wife's voice on the radio changes his mind.
He goes down with the boat.
Reality TV Crew
A reality TV show wants to film your station for a season. The command loves the idea. You're asked to be a featured swimmer. What do you do?
You come off as funny and competent. Recruiting loves it.
Stay off camera
Quiet professional. Your mom is disappointed.
Your spouse is tired of the moves and the 3 AM launches. They want you out when your enlistment ends. What do you do?
You become a city firefighter. Home for dinner most nights.
Reenlist anyway
Your spouse adapts. Mostly.
Divorce papers arrive by spring.
Ask for a stable billet
Four years at one station. Your family settles in.
No stable billets available.
Chief's Board
You're up for chief petty officer. Your record is solid, but your evaluations have one bad mark from a feud with an old supervisor. What do you do?
Get letters of support
Promoted to chief. Fouled anchors on your collar.
Not this year.
Let your record speak
Promoted. The bad mark didn't matter.
The bad mark mattered.
Medevac From a Tanker
A tanker crewman has chest pain 150 miles out. The deck is covered in pipes and cables. There's barely a hoist spot. What do you do?
Hoist to the bow
Tight, but you land clean and package him fast.
You snag a cable on the way down.
Ship lowers him by boat
Creative and safe.
The boat launch takes an hour. He gets worse.
Breaking In a Rookie
Your new junior swimmer froze on his first live case and the survivor waited an extra minute. He's crushed. What do you do?
Share your first case
He laughs at your story. He's solid on his next case.
Hard retraining
Brutal pool sessions. He never freezes again.
He requests reassignment.
By the book. He resents you.
Into the Outer Bands
As aircraft commander of an MH-60 Jayhawk, you're asked to launch into a hurricane's outer bands for a sinking sailboat. What do you do?
The worst flight of your life. Everyone aboard the sailboat lives.
Severe turbulence throws the crew around. You turn back.
Wait for a weather gap
A gap opens. Clean rescue.
The boat sinks. A cutter finds survivors in a raft hours later.
You've hit bingo fuel. One last survivor is in the water, 100 yards away. Another hoist means landing on fumes. What do you do?
One more hoist
You land with minutes of fuel left. Survivor saved.
You make a precautionary landing on a beach. Survivor still saved.
He climbs in the raft. A second helo gets him.
He never reaches the raft.
Night rescue in fog with a new copilot. His voice is shaking on the intercom and his callouts are late. What do you do?
Calm him, keep him in
He settles. He nails the approach. He'll never forget it.
Take the controls
You fly it yourself. He's quiet the whole way home.
Flying an MH-65 Dolphin, you need to hover 20 feet over a swaying cliff face so your swimmer can reach a fallen climber. What do you do?
Hold the hover
Rock steady. The swimmer reaches him. The crew calls it the best hover they've seen.
A gust pushes the rotor close to the cliff. You abort.
Extra distance keeps the rotors safe.
The swinging line delays the rescue.
As operations officer, you must decide whether to launch a second helicopter in bad weather. One crew is already out. What do you do?
Launch backup
Smart. The first crew has a mechanical issue and the backup finishes the rescue.
The second aircraft has to divert too.
The first crew finishes alone.
You're flying a drug interdiction mission. A go-fast boat won't stop. Your gunner is ready to disable the engines. What do you do?
Disable the engines
Precision shots. The boat stops. 2 tons of cocaine seized.
A shot ricochets near the crew. Investigation.
Keep tracking
A cutter intercepts.
The boat escapes into foreign waters.
You spot an overloaded migrant vessel heading toward Florida. The weather is turning. Interdiction or rescue? What do you do?
Rescue first
Lives saved. Policy questions later.
Shadow and call a cutter
The cutter arrives in time.
The boat capsizes before the cutter arrives.
You just took command of an air station after a brutal hurricane season. Swimmers are limping and mechs are sleeping in the hangar. What do you do?
Mandatory rest rotation
Readiness dips for a week, then climbs higher than before.
Push through the season
Everyone makes it to winter in one piece.
A fatigued swimmer gets hurt on a routine hoist. It's on you.
Borrow crews from nearby
Another station sends a crew. Your people finally sleep.
They're stretched too. Request denied.
Hoist Mishap Board
A swimmer broke his leg during a hoist on a flight you commanded. The mishap board wants your statement. You made a timing error. What do you do?
Own the error
Your honesty leads to a new hoist-timing procedure fleet-wide.
Blame the sea state
The board accepts it.
The flight data recorder tells a different story.
Hours or Parts
Your station's budget was cut mid-year. You can protect flight training hours or spare-parts funding, not both. What do you choose?
Spare parts
Aircraft stay flyable. Pilots grumble about lost hours.
Training hours
Crews stay razor sharp and the parts hold out.
A helicopter sits grounded during a big case.
Live at Five
After a dramatic cliff rescue, a national news anchor wants you live on air in an hour. Your swimmer did the real work. What do you do?
Go on and credit the crew
You name all four crew members. Great PR for the Coast Guard.
Send the swimmer
He's awkward but charming. His mom watches it 40 times.
A major hurricane just made landfall. Hundreds of 911 calls are pouring in from rooftops. You have four helicopters. How do you prioritize?
Grid the city by zone
Systematic sweeps. Your crews pull 180 people off roofs in two days.
Communications fail and zones get duplicated.
Chase 911 calls
Fast response to the worst cases.
Crews burn fuel flying across the city.
Night Water Landing
Your Jayhawk loses an engine 40 miles offshore at night. You might make the coast on one engine, or you could ditch now. What do you do?
Limp for the coast
You land on a beach with nothing left. The crew hugs on the sand.
killed in a helicopter ditching
The second engine overheats over the water.
Controlled ditching
Textbook ditching. Everyone gets out. Another helo picks you up.
The aircraft rolls fast. You barely get out.
Flare Gun Hoax
Your crew has launched three times this month for fake mayday calls from the same area. Another one just came in. What do you do?
Launch anyway
It's real this time. A father and son on a sinking skiff.
Delay to verify
It's another hoax. Investigators trace the caller.
It was real. The delay cost a life.
Bering Sea Deployment
You're flying off a cutter in the Bering Sea for two months. The deck is pitching wildly for your landing. What do you do?
Wait for a quiet period
The deck settles for five seconds. You land perfectly.
You orbit until fuel forces a hard landing.
Land on the next roll
Smooth landing.
The deck rises fast. A hard landing damages the gear.
Ensign's Mistake
A junior officer signed off on an aircraft that wasn't properly inspected. Nobody was hurt. He confesses to you. What do you do?
Teach, document lightly
He becomes the most careful officer at the station.
Formal report
By the book. His career takes a hit.
Your crew rescued a migrant family from a sinking raft. The mother begs you not to send them back. Policy says repatriation. What do you do?
Follow policy, kindly
You make sure they're fed and treated with dignity. It still hurts.
Report medical needs
The child's illness requires a hospital ashore.
Medical clears them. Repatriation proceeds.
After 72 hours searching for a missing fisherman, survival odds are near zero. His wife begs you to keep searching. It's your call. What do you do?
Suspend the search
You tell her in person. The hardest conversation of your career.
One more day
Unbelievably, he's found alive on a buoy.
Nothing. The extra day costs fuel and crew rest.
A federal agency wants to take over a drug interdiction case your crew started. Their agent is demanding your crew's evidence. What do you do?
Joint operation. Big seizure. Good relationships.
Fight for the case
Coast Guard gets credit.
Turf war. Higher is annoyed.
Your best pilot is showing signs of burnout. He's short with his crew and making small errors. He refuses time off. What do you do?
Ground him for rest
He's angry at first. Two weeks later, he thanks you.
Let him fly
He pulls through.
A near-miss in the hangar. Investigation follows.
Your promotion board is next month. A staff job would help your record more than another flying tour. What do you do?
Promoted. You miss flying.
Not selected.
Promoted on operational merit.
Passed over.
A researcher on an Arctic ice camp needs an emergency evacuation. It's 300 miles away and storms are coming. What do you do?
Launch now
Long flight, frozen fuel lines, but you bring her home.
The storm forces you down at a remote village.
Coordinate a fixed-wing
An HC-130 with skis makes the pickup.
Delays make it a near thing.
Social Media Storm
A swimmer at your station posted a video mocking a rescued boater. It's going viral. What do you do?
Public apology
Swift response. Story dies in a day.
Quietly handle it
The story grows. Headquarters calls.
Medical Emergency Flight
A woman on a remote island is in labor with complications. The weather is marginal. The nearest hospital is 90 minutes away. What do you do?
You land just in time. Healthy baby.
Turbulent flight. The baby is born in the helicopter. Both fine.
Send a cutter
Slower, but safe. Mother and baby fine.
Three swimmers are caught in a rip current off a crowded beach. Lifeguards have one, but two are being pulled out. What do you do?
Deploy for both
You swim parallel, get both, and hoist them. Beach applauds.
You get one. A lifeguard gets the other.
Get the weaker swimmer
Smart triage. Lifeguards get the other.
Two fishermen you just hoisted start fighting in the cabin. One pulls a knife. What do you do?
Restrain him
You pin him down. The mech helps.
You get cut.
Talk them down
Calm prevails.
The fight escalates.
A pregnant woman is among survivors of a capsized boat. She's showing signs of labor and you're 45 minutes from shore. What do you do?
Prepare for delivery
Baby delivered in the helicopter. Both fine.
Complications. Hospital handles it.
Calm her, fly fast
She makes it to the hospital.
The baby comes in the cabin anyway.
A kayaker is pinned against a rock in a flooded river. The water is fast and full of debris. What do you do?
Rappel from helo
Perfect placement. Kayaker freed.
Debris hits you.
Swiftwater approach
You reach him.
The current pins you too.
An old shoulder injury is getting worse. A medical board could end your flying career. What do you do?
Get surgery
Six months rehab. You return.
It holds.
It tears during a rescue.
During a flood, a family begs you to save their dog stuck on a roof. You have room but limited fuel. What do you do?
Save the dog
The family cries with joy. Local news loves it.
Fuel saved. The family is heartbroken.
A hiker in a canyon has heat stroke. It's 115 degrees. Your helicopter can't land. What do you do?
Hoist down to him
You cool him and hoist. He survives.
The heat gets you too.
Drop water, wait
Ground team gets him.
Too late.
Your mentor, a legendary chief swimmer, is retiring. You're asked to speak. What do you say?
Funny stories
The room roars.
He cries.
A ferry is sinking in a storm with 60 passengers. Multiple helicopters are responding. You're the first swimmer on scene. What do you do?
Organize life rafts
You organize passengers into rafts. Most survive.
Chaos. Some lost.
Hoist the injured
Critical cases saved first.
Others drift away.
You've done 12 hoists today in a hurricane. Your arms barely work. Another case drops. What do you do?
Somehow, you do it.
Your body gives out in the water.
Tell the crew you're done
Another swimmer takes it. Smart.
During a night rescue, your hoist cable snaps and your partner swimmer is in the water alone. What do you do?
Drop a raft and stay
Another helo arrives. Both rescued.
Jump in to help
You stay together until rescue.
Hypothermia sets in for both of you.
Kids in the Lake
Two kids fell through ice on a frozen pond. One is under the ice. Time is critical. What do you do?
Go under the ice
You find him under the ice. He survives.
drowned under the ice during a rescue
You lose your way under the ice.
Get the visible kid first
One saved. Divers get the other.
The other child doesn't survive.
As {rank}, you command a Coast Guard district. Budget planners want to close an air station. You must testify. What do you do?
Air station saved.
It closes anyway.
Propose consolidation
A compromise saves money and most capability.
The Dolphins are aging fast. You're asked to recommend a replacement strategy. What do you push?
Bigger, more capable fleet.
New aircraft
Funded. The future is bright.
Program stalls in Congress.
Hurricane Response Lead
A Category 5 hurricane is heading for a major city. You coordinate the entire Coast Guard response. What's your priority?
Preposition assets
Helicopters are ready the moment winds drop. Thousands rescued.
Evacuate stations first
Assets safe. Response slightly delayed.
A senator questions why a search was suspended too early. A family is in the room. What do you say?
Explain with empathy
The family appreciates your honesty.
Defend the policy
Technically correct. Coldly received.
After 30 years, you're retiring. Your crew offers you one last flight. Do you take it?
Fly it
A perfect sunset flight. The crew sprays you with water on landing.
Retire quietly
You slip away with dignity.
Aviators' Memorial
You dedicate a memorial to Coast Guard aviators lost in the line of duty. Widows and grown children fill the front rows. What do you say?
It takes 15 minutes. A helicopter flies over as you read the last one. Nobody moves.
Tell one crew's story
You tell how one crew flew into a storm for strangers. Every family feels it.
Women make up a tiny share of rescue swimmers, and A-School attrition is brutal for everyone. You're asked to fix the pipeline. What do you do?
Pre-A-School prep program
Same standards, better prep. Graduation rates climb for everyone.
Funding gets stuck for two years.
Mentorship network
Senior swimmers coach candidates. Numbers slowly improve.
A watchdog report calls out your district by name.
Border Mission Creep
At a homeland security summit, other agencies want your rescue helicopters for border surveillance. Your crews are already stretched. What do you say?
Protect the rescue mission
You hold the line. Search and rescue stays the priority.
You're overruled from above.
Agree to share hours
Better relations. Your crews fly a lot more nights.
Old Swimmer Calls
A retired swimmer you once commanded calls you. He's struggling with PTSD, lost his job, and sounds like he's been drinking. What do you do?
Drive over now
You sit with him until morning and get him into a VA program. He's okay.
Send him resources
He thanks you, flatly. You think about him for weeks.
Two hoist mishaps in one month across your district. A full safety stand-down would pause training flights for a week. What do you do?
Order the stand-down
Crews find three bad habits. No more mishaps that year.
Targeted review only
The review finds a worn cable batch. Fixed.
A third mishap. Now headquarters orders the stand-down.
Melting ice is bringing cruise ships and tankers into the Arctic. The nearest rescue helicopter is 900 miles away. What do you push for?
Seasonal forward bases
Summer detachments in remote Alaska cut response times by hours.
Fuel and housing costs kill the plan.
More icebreakers
Slow, expensive, and steady progress.
Jayhawk Night Hoist
Your Jayhawk is hovering over a rolling fishing boat at night. Your swimmer is on deck but the boat's antenna is swinging toward the cable. What do you do?
Hold and wait for a lull
You hold a perfect hover for 90 seconds. Three fishermen up.
The antenna snags the cable. You shear it with the cable cutter.
Move to a water pickup
Fishermen jump and your swimmer collects them. Slower but safe.
Lost Hikers Overnight
Two hikers are lost in fog-covered mountains. Your thermal camera might find them, but terrain clearance is tight. Do you search tonight?
Search with thermal
Two heat signatures on a ridge. Both hikers hoisted, cold but alive.
Fog thickens. You turn back empty-handed.
Wait for first light
You find them at dawn huddled under a tarp.
One doesn't survive the night.
Copilot's Complaint
A junior pilot reports that a senior aircraft commander has been making demeaning comments to her on flights. He's well liked. What do you do?
Report and investigate
The investigation confirms it. The crew room gets healthier.
Talk to him informally
He apologizes and changes.
It continues. Now you're part of the complaint.
Not a Real Military
At a family reunion, your uncle says the Coast Guard isn't a 'real' military. Everyone's watching. What do you do?
He still doesn't get it. Your cousin does, though.
Tell a rescue story
The table goes quiet. Your uncle buys you a beer.
Kid's Question
A kid at an air show asks if you've ever been scared in the water. What do you tell him?
'Every single time'
His mom smiles. The kid looks even more impressed.
Drowning Prevention Swim
A charity open-water swim raises money for kids' swim lessons. It's cold and two miles. Do you join?
You finish near the front and teach a kid to float afterward.
Your money pays for a summer of lessons.
The crew watches a Coast Guard rescue movie. It's dramatic and wildly inaccurate. {buddy} is shouting at the screen. Join in?
Shout too
Best night of the month.
You secretly love it.
Off-Duty Beach Day
Off duty at the beach, you see a young lifeguard struggling with a panicked swimmer twice his size. What do you do?
Swim out and help
You get behind the swimmer and help tow him in. The lifeguard thanks you.
You swallow half the ocean, but you both get him in.
Watch from shore
The lifeguard manages. You feel guilty all afternoon.
A guy at the gym challenges you to a pull-up contest. He has a camera rolling. Do you accept?
He wins. The video gets 2 million views.
You finish your workout in peace.
Linked arms in the 58-degree Coronado surf at 0400. Your teeth are chattering so hard you bit your tongue. The instructor offers hot coffee to anyone who quits. What will you do?
Stay in the water
You stayed. Hypothermic, purple, and still in the class.
You went hypothermic and got pulled by medical. Rolled back a class.
Take the coffee
You rang the bell. The coffee was lukewarm.
Hell Week Day 3
Hell Week, day three. You have slept 45 minutes total. Your boat crew is hallucinating. {buddy} wants to quit. What will you do?
Carry him through it
You talked him through the night. You both secured Hell Week. Brothers for life.
He rang the bell anyway. You keep going without him.
Focus on yourself
You survived. He quit. You wonder if you could have helped.
Your shins are fractured. Every step is lightning. The bell is 30 feet away and it would all stop. What will you do?
Hide the injury
You gutted it out. The fracture healed crooked, but you made it.
You collapsed on a run. Medically rolled back. Six months more.
Report to medical
Medically rolled. You will start again with the next class.
Three rings. It is over. You will think about it forever.
Hands and feet tied, you must bob in the 9-foot pool for 5 minutes. You are sinking more than bobbing. What will you do?
Relax and trust it
You found the rhythm. Passed.
You panicked and inhaled water. The instructor fished you out. Retest next week.
Fight the water
You thrashed through it and passed somehow.
You blacked out. Pulled out by safety divers.
An instructor orders you to get wet and sandy for a smudge on your boot. Again. The sand is in places sand should never be. What will you do?
Smile and comply
You rolled in the sand like a happy dog. He moved on to someone else.
Argue about the smudge
Your entire boat crew got wet and sandy. They will remember this.
Pool competency: instructors rip off your mask, tie your air hoses in knots, and shut off your valve underwater. What will you do?
Calmly fix each problem
You worked the procedures with burning lungs. Passed on the first try.
You bolted for the surface. Fail. Next attempt in two days.
Surface immediately
Automatic fail. Almost half your class failed too.
Your boat crew is carrying a 200 lb log. The shortest guy on the crew is not touching it. What will you do?
Call him out
He got the message and started pulling his weight.
The instructor punished the whole crew for "drama."
Take the extra weight
Your shoulder is screaming. The instructors noticed you.
